messages:
alex: Quick sync — I pushed a tiny rewrite of the Python streaming example to address backpressure wording in the SDK guide. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4789 :eyes:

tara: Nice. Does it also update the pagination example in TS? That's where we had the stale `cursor` -> `resume_token` rename.

bob: (docs-bot) CI passed for #4789 — link checks OK, linter flagged one line length.

alex: Good catch. I only updated py and the conceptual note. I can either update TS and Go in this PR or split into three tiny PRs. Thoughts?

ben: Split would be easier to review quickly. Small PR per language + one PR for the migration note.

kevin: Agreed. If you split, please include the short test snippet I mentioned for retry jitter, otherwise we miss the flakiness fix. Example: ```python
# retry backoff sample
for attempt in range(3):
    try:
        stream = client.responses.stream(... )
        break
    except TransientError:
        time.sleep(0.2 * 2 ** attempt + random.random() * 0.05)
```

alex: I'll split. Plan: #4789 -> Python (already merged), new PRs: TS (WIP) and Go (WIP), and a small cross-lang migration note linking them. I'll include Kevin's jitter snippet in all three.

tara: For TS, remember to show both callback and async iterator patterns. Some users only skim one style. Also update the inline link to the pagination spec (it currently points to old internal doc).

alex: Good call. Can someone volunteer to sanity-check the TS snippet? I can do Go if no objections.

ben: I can take TS tonight. Will also replace the old pagination link with https://github.com/redwood-inference/specs/pagination (that new spec has the token schema).

kevin: When you update TS please add a short note about stream cancellation to avoid leaked connections. Example line: `controller.abort()` in the iterator example.

alex: Solid. Ben — can you add that to your PR? Also add `@tara` as reviewer and tag `docs-easy` label for faster merge.

ben: Yup. I'll open PR shortly: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4810 (TS) and add reviewers.

alex: I'll open Go PR: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4811 and add Kevin for the jitter snippet review.

tara: Tiny request — can we also add a single combined code sandbox that shows py/ts/go side-by-side for the migration note? That helped last time.

ben: I can assemble a one-page markdown with inline code blocks and push to the migration note PR. Keeps things discoverable.

alex: Perfect. I'll update the migration note to link to the sandbox and add a short `Troubleshooting` section about timeouts vs retries.

kevin: One more: add a compatibility table for older SDK versions (v0.9, v1.0) so users know which snippet to use.

alex: On it. I'll add a small table and a note: "If you're on <v1.0, use legacy cursor param".

ben: OK I'm opening the TS PR now and pinging @tara. Will post link here when done.

alex: Thanks all — leaving this thread open until both PRs are merged. Ping if you hit blocker. :thumbsup:
